query: Super Micro liquid cooled AI rack shipments growth
normalized: ai cooled growth liquid micro rack shipments super

output.content:
Super Micro does not disclose a stand-alone quarterly or annual **liquid-cooled AI-rack shipment growth rate**, so its reported figures should be interpreted primarily as delivery milestones and production capacity rather than a clean shipment series. [[1]] 

The clearest reported progression is: more than 2,000 liquid-cooled racks delivered since June 2024, 2,000+ DLC racks per month of production capacity in fiscal Q3 2025, and 2,000 DLC racks per month in fiscal Q4 2025. [[2]] [[3]] [[4]] 

Management’s FY2026 manufacturing target was up to 6,000 total racks per month, including 3,000 DLC-optimized racks per month; relative to the 2,000-per-month DLC rate cited in FY2025, that implies a planned **50% increase in liquid-cooling rack capacity**. [[5]] [[4]] 

The broader AI-rack demand backdrop was strong: FY2025 net sales were $21.972 billion versus $14.989 billion in FY2024, while GPU and Super Rack billings increased by $5.804 billion, or 52% year over year; however, that category includes both liquid- and air-cooled systems, so it cannot be treated as liquid-cooled-rack shipment growth specifically. [[1]] 

The key investment takeaway is that Super Micro’s liquid-cooled AI-rack expansion was substantial—capacity moved from a 2,000-per-month run rate in FY2025 toward 3,000 per month in FY2026—but reported evidence supports a **capacity-ramp thesis**, not a precisely measurable DLC shipment-growth percentage. [[4]] [[5]]
